audit_scope.description: This batch primarily covers EL logic: EVM precompiles (BLAKE2), transaction processing (Prague TX types, EIP-1559 conversion), blob gas pricing (EIP-7762), P2P networking (EIP-8 RLPx), and RPC verification (EIP-7919). Several governance-only EIPs (EIP-7329, EIP-2378, EIP-7199) have no protocol runtime impact.

misclassified_entities.reason: EIP-7329 is a governance/meta EIP about repository organization. No protocol runtime impact. Entity is part of off-chain governance, not a security-relevant external entity.
EIP-7329 Documentation User interacts with a static website, not the Ethereum protocol. Not a security-relevant external entity.
EIP-2378 is a governance process EIP. The EIP Author interacts with off-chain governance, not the protocol runtime.
EIP-7199 is a meta-governance EIP about linting rules. No protocol runtime impact.
Internal component: transaction execution (EVM) is part of the EL itself, not an external entity. It produces receipts as an internal process.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer via P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block producers submit blocks via the P2P network. Any peer can propose blocks with arbitrary header values including excess_blob_gas. All header fields must be independently validated. No authentication on P2P layer.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any user or dapp can submit raw transaction bytes via unauthenticated JSON-RPC. Transactions may be malformed, have invalid signatures, insufficient gas, or attempt DoS. Covers EXT-CALLER (precompile calls originate from transactions), EXT-USER-OR-DAPP (EIP-3709 wallet-side conversion), EXT-TX-SUBMITTER, EXT-TX-SIGNER, and EXT-USER (ETH sender).

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via devp2p/RLPx
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Remote peers connect via TCP and perform RLPx handshakes (EIP-8). Any network entity can attempt connections with arbitrary protocol versions, malformed packets, or unknown packet types. ECIES encryption authenticates the static key but does not imply trust in data content. Covers EXT-PEER-INITIATOR and EXT-REMOTE-PEER.

trusted_external_entities.name: Discovery Peer via UDP
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Discovery packets arrive via unauthenticated UDP. Any network entity can send packets up to 1280 bytes with unknown types or malformed data. Source IP can be spoofed. No authentication whatsoever.

trusted_external_entities.name: Third-Party RPC Provider
trusted_external_entities.rationale: RPC providers return blockchain data that may be incorrect or malicious. EIP-7919 introduces proof-based verification specifically because providers cannot be trusted. Light clients must verify all responses against known state roots.

trusted_external_entities.name: Light Client via RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Light clients query logs and data. While typically benign, query patterns could be used for resource exhaustion. No authentication required for public RPC endpoints.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: All block header fields must be independently recalculated and validated. The excess_blob_gas field must match calc_excess_blob_gas() output. Fork activation timestamp boundary must be correctly detected for one-time reset.

Full transaction validation required: signature verification (ECDSA recovery with low-s enforcement), nonce checks, gas sufficiency (intrinsic + EIP-7623 floor), init code size limits, transaction type detection and type-specific decoding. For precompile calls (BLAKE2 at 0x09): input length must be exactly 213 bytes, final flag must be 0 or 1, gas cost = rounds * GFROUND.

Auth packets must be ECIES-decryptable with recipient's static key. Required fields (signature, nonces, public keys) must be present. Version checks are intentionally skipped for forward compatibility. Extra RLP elements and trailing data are ignored. Hello packets parsed tolerantly per Postel's Law. Random padding (100-300 bytes) required for traffic analysis resistance.

Packets must not exceed 1280 bytes. Unknown packet types must be silently discarded. Tolerant RLP parsing ignoring version and extra elements. No trust in source IP (spoofable). Rate limiting recommended to prevent amplification attacks.

All RPC responses must be verified against cryptographic proofs anchored to known state roots. SSZ Merkle proofs must validate data correctness and completeness. No data should be trusted without proof verification. Provider-supplied data without valid proof must be rejected.
Query processing must be bounded to prevent resource exhaustion. Log responses should include completeness proofs when available. Rate limiting on public endpoints recommended.
